intro: You've been putting up with a cramped, awkward bathroom for years — maybe it's a tight corner shower tray that's seen better days, or a layout in your older Whitehill home that just doesn't work anymore. A wet room installation changes all of that. Rather than a raised tray and a curtain or screen, a wet room gives you a fully waterproofed, level-access shower space that's easier to clean, looks genuinely impressive, and adds real value to your property. For homeowners across Whitehill, this is increasingly the upgrade of choice when budgets allow for doing things properly — and when it's done right, it can last decades without issue.
localContext: Whitehill sits in Midlothian and has a mix of property types that each come with their own considerations for wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up a good portion of the town's housing stock tend to have solid floors, thick walls, and older plumbing layouts — all of which need careful assessment before any work begins. Timber suspended floors, which do appear in some of the older homes here, require specific tanking and drainage approaches to ensure the waterproofing holds long-term. The newer modern estates in Whitehill are generally more straightforward to work with, but every job still needs a proper survey. Whitehill is also in a moderately hard water area, which matters for wet rooms — limescale can build up on drains, linear channels, and glass surfaces over time, so choosing fittings designed to handle this, and staying on top of descaling, will protect your investment and keep everything looking clean.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation is a multi-stage project that takes most experienced tradespeople around four to seven days depending on the size of the space and what they find when they open up the room. The process in a Whitehill property typically starts with a thorough survey — checking the floor structure, existing drainage, pipework runs, and whether the walls can support the tanking system without issues. Once that's signed off, the existing bathroom fittings are stripped out and the floor is prepared to create the correct fall towards the drain, which is critical for water to clear properly rather than pooling. The entire wet zone — floor and walls to a suitable height — is then tanked with a waterproof membrane system, often a combination of liquid tanking and reinforced tape at joins and corners. This stage is where quality really matters; a rushed tanking job is the number one cause of wet room failures years down the line. After tanking cures, the tiler works across floor and walls before plumbing fixtures are fitted — including the drain, shower valve, and any heated towel rail or underfloor heating if specified. A final seal around fittings and a thorough check completes the job. Throughout this process in Whitehill, tradespeople who know the local property stock will flag issues early rather than letting surprises drive up costs mid-job.
pricing: In Whitehill, a straightforward wet room conversion in a standard-sized bathroom typically falls between £6,000 and £9,000, with more complex projects — larger rooms, structural floor work, full tiling packages, or high-spec fixtures — running from £9,000 up to £12,000 or beyond. The older stone-built properties and period cottages in Whitehill sometimes carry higher costs due to unexpected findings like uneven floors needing significant levelling, outdated pipework that needs upgrading, or walls that require additional prep before tanking. Modern estate homes tend to sit at the lower end of the range. Material choices make a significant difference too — a quality linear drain and large-format porcelain tiles cost considerably more than basic alternatives, but they're worth it for longevity.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Whitehill and the surrounding Midlothian area makes a genuine difference on a project like this. They'll have worked in similar properties — whether that's the older stone-built homes or newer builds on the modern estates — and they'll know what to expect when walls come off or floors get opened up. Local tradespeople also have established relationships with local suppliers, which helps when materials need to be sourced quickly or when something unexpected requires a fast solution. For a premium, high-value installation in Whitehill, working with someone who understands the area is simply less risky than bringing in an unknown quantity.

faqs.q: Will a wet room work in an older stone-built property in Whitehill?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it needs careful planning. Older stone-built homes in Whitehill often have solid floors, which are actually ideal for wet rooms as they're stable and don't flex. The key is thorough tanking and making sure any existing damp issues are resolved before work begins. A proper survey before the job starts will identify anything that needs addressing.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Whitehill?
faqs.a: Most standard wet room installations in Whitehill take between four and seven working days, assuming no major structural surprises. Larger bathrooms, more complex tiling layouts, or older properties that need extra prep work can push this closer to eight to ten days. Your tradesperson should give you a realistic timeline after the initial survey rather than a rushed estimate.

faqs.q: Does the moderately hard water in Whitehill cause problems for wet rooms?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water does mean limescale will gradually build up on drains, glass screens, and chrome fittings if left untreated. It's not a dealbreaker, but it's worth choosing a linear drain that's easy to remove and clean, using a daily shower spray to slow limescale build-up, and descaling fittings a few times a year. Some homeowners in Whitehill also opt for a water softener if it's a bigger concern.

faqs.q: Can I add underfloor heating to a wet room in Whitehill?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's a popular addition in Whitehill — particularly in the older properties where bathrooms can feel cold in winter. Electric underfloor heating mats are the most common option as they're relatively simple to install within the floor build-up before tiling. It adds to the project cost but genuinely improves day-to-day comfort, especially in a fully tiled space that would otherwise feel cold underfoot.
